search_record.question: What foundational literatures own perfect-information value, context-conditioned policy choice, offline contextual-policy evaluation, adaptive versus nonadaptive policy value, and heterogeneous policy learning?
search_record.conclusion: The executed ORF calculation is a scorer-specific deterministic application of established perfect-information/policy-class value. Contextual bandits and policy learning study the harder missing step: choosing actions from observable context and evaluating a learned policy. Adaptive-submodularity work further distinguishes adaptive policies from fixed choices under partial observability. No general regret-concept novelty is tenable.

papers.title: Information Value Theory
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics, 2(1), 22–26
papers.core_contribution: Develops a decision-analytic value-of-information theory in which information is valued through the consequences of decisions rather than probability alone.
papers.methodology: Compares decision value before and after resolving uncertainty; perfect information is the limiting case relevant to an oracle that sees all counterfactual action values.
papers.key_results: Establishes the decision-theoretic information-value framing that owns the conceptual form of max-after-information versus max-before-information.
papers.relevance_reason: Closest conceptual foundation: ORF's sum of row-wise maxima versus one shared maximum is a deterministic perfect-information value calculation.

papers.title: The Epoch-Greedy Algorithm for Multi-armed Bandits with Side Information
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 20
papers.core_contribution: Introduces Epoch-Greedy for bandits with observable side information, connecting action choice from context to a supervised policy class and regret.
papers.methodology: Alternates exploration with greedy use of a learned context-to-action rule and bounds regret through the hypothesis class's sample complexity.
papers.key_results: Reports regret scaling of O(T^(2/3) S^(1/3)) or better, where S is the supervised-learning complexity term.
papers.relevance_reason: Shows the operational distinction ORF does not test: selecting actions from observed context rather than from full counterfactual scores.

warnings: The proceedings landing-page title says 'side information'; the PDF title uses 'contextual multi-armed bandits'. The report uses the proceedings title.

papers.title: Doubly Robust Policy Evaluation and Learning
papers.core_contribution: Studies contextual-policy evaluation and optimization from historical data with partially observed rewards using doubly robust estimation.
papers.methodology: Combines a reward model with a past-policy model so value estimation remains accurate when either component is well specified.
papers.key_results: Provides accuracy guarantees under either a good reward model or a good logging-policy model and reports lower-variance evaluation and better learned policies.
papers.relevance_reason: Makes explicit that an operational conditional policy needs observable context, logged action data, and policy evaluation—none supplied by the ORF oracle table.

papers.title: Adaptive Submodularity: Theory and Applications in Active Learning and Stochastic Optimization
papers.core_contribution: Formalizes adaptive submodularity for sequential choices under partial observability and derives guarantees for adaptive greedy policies.
papers.methodology: Compares policies that condition later actions on observed item states with nonadaptive selections and characterizes when greedy adaptation is competitive.
papers.key_results: Provides approximation guarantees for adaptive stochastic maximization and coverage and analyzes adaptivity gaps in its problem class.
papers.relevance_reason: Foundational precedent for separating the value of an adaptive policy from a fixed policy under observations; ORF instead grants perfect counterfactual observability.

papers.title: Policy Learning With Observational Data
papers.core_contribution: Learns constrained treatment-assignment policies from observational data using semiparametrically efficient, doubly robust scores.
papers.methodology: Optimizes a policy class over observable individual characteristics under identification assumptions and application constraints.
papers.key_results: Establishes asymptotic utilitarian-regret guarantees for the learned policy.
papers.relevance_reason: A mature analogue of heterogeneous action assignment versus one uniform action; unlike ORF, it addresses learned policy value and identification.
